english: Man, will you buy my grey (mare) horse? I will not buy her; my child rides her. Then what will you buy? These two young horses. What will you give me? Ten cows and ten sheep. The price is good/worthy. Drive the two young ones (?) and feed those two well.

Carpenter, from what wood do you build wheels? I build them from oak wood. It is firm. How many days do you work? Four days. Now I yoke the oxen to the new wagon. Will you work for me? I will work for you, and gladly / I am used to it.

Of the white ones, my lord, the horses are swifter than yours. Friend, your words are bold. Did you not fear my team/yoking? I did not fear it. We drive to the river by the oak. Whoever wins takes the prize. What is the prize? My red foal of a horse. The gods watch us. Go!
uncertain: pérkʷum déh₂newi 'to the oak, to the river'?

english: Grandmother, what is the wheel of the sun? The sun is a wheel of fire. It turns across the day. Who draws that wagon? Tawny horses draw it. Do you see the sun? I see it, and my eye burns. Now do not look at the sun. Look at the foals in the field.
uncertain: sh₂wéns read as gen of sun

english: Mother, what is a yoke? A yoke is wood that joins two oxen. What is the axle? The axle stands between the wheels; the wheels turn around it. Shall I show you the wagon? Show it to me. Shall I sit? Sit and take the rope. Do not drive it.
uncertain: h₁íd mē déwks 'do not pull it'

english: Grandfather, why does the wagon go slowly? The axle is drying out. Bring me fat. Here is fat. Where shall I smear it? Smear it on the axle at the wheels. Do you see? Now the wheels turn. They turn. Now the oxen pull the wagon quickly.
